text:
jess: heads up — some eu-west customers reporting TLS cert mismatch after last night's cert rotation. ALB serving internal wildcard instead of customer-host cert for a subset of requests.

anil: hmm, similar symptoms to a listener / rule ordering problem we saw months ago. did the acm rotate multiple certs at once?

maya: deploy logs show two ACM certificates were active during the window (old + new) and we pushed a change to contour's tlsconfig at 1792345900.

ev an: quick check — are the failing clients behind our NAT pool? iirc some egress proxies strip SNI on older devices.

jess: verified -- failing requests originate from the nat-egress-* pool (10.20.x.x) and from a subset of health-check IPs. tcpdump shows ClientHello without SNI for those IPs.

ops-bot: deploy finished for service/ingress-controller at 1792346000 :white_check_mark:

anil: if clienthello lacks SNI, ALB will fall back to a default cert (usually the first listener/priority match). do we have a legacy listener with a default cert?

maya: yes — there is a legacy listener that we left for canary traffic (listener-8080-legacy) created manually long ago. it has a wildcard internal cert. contour also created a listener with the tenant cert. priorities might be conflicting.

evan: ALB behavior: if multiple rules match, it uses rule priority and then default cert if SNI absent. if legacy listener has higher priority (lower number) it can win for SNI-less handshakes.

jess: reproducer below (from a failing node):
```
# shows no sni -> fallback cert
openssl s_client -connect alb-eu-west.internal:443 -prexit -brief < /dev/null | grep "subject="
# force sni
openssl s_client -connect alb-eu-west.internal:443 -servername tenant.prod.example.com < /dev/null | sed -n '1,8p'
```

anil: nice. so two immediate mitigations: 1) remove the manual legacy listener / ensure its priority is lower, 2) tighten NAT egress so probes preserve SNI (or route health-checks via a SNI-capable source).

maya: i'm going to open infra ticket to remove legacy listener and add a CIDR tag to the nat pool so we can route health checks through the correct egress.

ops-bot: ticket INFRA-3121 created by maya: "Remove legacy ALB listener and re-run cert rotation"

jess: also worth adding a rollout check in our cert rotation playbook: after update, sample from each egress pool + health-check IPs and validate presented cert matches SNI -> fail and rollback otherwise.

evan: +1. will add a quick script to the rotation job that runs openssl s_client from a small set of internal probes (nat-egress, health-checks, canary nodes).

anil: one more note: if we can't immediately remove the listener, we can temporarily attach the tenant cert to the legacy listener as well (same cert) so SNI-less clients get the correct cert until NAT changes land. risk = duplicates in ACM, but workable short-term.

maya: ack. i'll do the listener removal during next maintenance window if greenlight from oncall. leaving this thread for runbook updates and postmortem notes. :memo:
